# The Tale of the First Echo

Long ago, when the world was newly formed, a lonely mountain spirit named Kora dwelled in silence among the peaks. She had witnessed the birth of rivers and the growth of forests, but had never heard her own voice, for sound itself had not yet learned to return.

One day, Kora sang out in her solitude, pouring her heart into a melody of longing. The sound traveled across the valleys and canyons, touching every stone and cliff face. The rocks, moved by her beautiful sorrow, decided to offer her a gift.

"We cannot give you companionship," whispered the ancient stones, "but we can give you company."

From that moment, they learned to catch her voice and send it back to her. When Kora sang again, she heard herself returning—not quite the same, but familiar and comforting.

Overjoyed, Kora sang every day, and the mountains faithfully returned her songs. Soon, all the cliffs and caves of the world learned this trick, offering comfort to the lonely and wonder to wanderers.

This is why, even now, when you call out to the mountains, they call back—a gift from the stones to remind us that we are never truly alone.

# The Tale of the First Shadow

In the beginning, when the world was newly formed, there lived a young weaver named Selene who possessed an unusual gift—she cast no shadow. While others moved through the day accompanied by their dark companions, Selene walked alone, and this made her deeply sad.

One evening, she climbed the highest mountain to plead with the Sun. "Great light-giver," she called, "why have you denied me a shadow like everyone else?"

The Sun replied warmly, "Dear child, I gave everyone else their shadows. But you—you were meant to create your own."

Confused, Selene descended the mountain. She gathered the darkest threads she could find: midnight's wool, raven's down, and the silk of deep caves. For seven days and nights, she wove at her loom, pouring her loneliness and longing into every knot.

On the eighth morning, as the Sun rose, Selene held up her creation. The woven cloth fell to the ground, and there it stayed—the world's first shadow, born not from light's absence, but from love's presence.

From that day forward, shadows were not merely cast but earned, each one a testament to the soul that created it.
